1.mascotDialogue: Once the expression becomes a tree, evaluating it is simple — solve both children, then apply the operator at the parent. No precedence table required at evaluation time. The shape already encodes it.

2.mascotDialogue: Line 8 is the base case — a leaf simply returns its digit. Lines 9 and 10 recurse into both children before line 11 combines them. The bottom of the tree evaluates first, always.

3.mascotDialogue: Because plus sits beneath times, it is forced to resolve first — this is precedence, shown as depth in the tree, rather than a rule you are expected to memorise.

4.mascotDialogue: This bug hides well precisely because multiplication does not care about order. Swap the operator to subtraction in your head, and this identical shape begins to lie to you.
